issues.claim: для `Sum<int>` это `int.Zero` и сложение `int` / for `Sum<int>` it is `int.Zero` and `int` addition
issues.problem: `int` has no accessible member `Zero`. `Int32` implements `INumberBase<int>.Zero` explicitly, so `int.Zero` does not compile (CS0117). The explanation teaches a non-existent API.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: для `Sum<int>` это реализация `INumberBase<int>.Zero` (значение 0) и сложение `int`. / for `Sum<int>` it is the `INumberBase<int>.Zero` implementation (value 0) and `int` addition.

issues.problem: `INumber<T>` lives in `System.Numerics`, which is not among the implicit usings. With option b the snippet as shown has no `using System.Numerics;` and would not compile as is. The prompt asks 'with which option does the method compile'.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `using System.Numerics;` as the first line of `code.source`.

issues.claim: harness: none with noRunReason about the placeholder
issues.problem: The snippet needs only the BCL, and the executable-code rule prefers a runnable snippet for BCL-only code. The placeholder constraint is why it is not runnable, so this is a weak justification.
issues.suggestedFix: Acceptable if kept. Optionally keep `none` and state in noRunReason that the constraint is deliberately omitted because it is the answer.

issues.claim: документация предупреждает о трудно диагностируемых ошибках компиляции и выполнения / the documentation warns about hard to diagnose compile-time and run-time errors
issues.problem: The configure-language-version excerpt is cut off right after 'Using a C# language version newer than the version associated with your target...'. Neither the 'hard to diagnose' wording nor the C# 7.3 default for .NET Framework is visible in it. The wording cannot be confirmed.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften to: the documentation says a language version newer than the one associated with the target framework is not supported and may cause compile-time or run-time errors; for .NET Framework the default is C# 7.3. Confirm against the full page.

issues.problem: The excerpt covers how to write static abstract members in interfaces and generic math. It says nothing about runtime support or .NET Framework, so it does not support the claim it is cited for. The URL also redirects to a different page.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the URL to the redirect target, or cite it only as the description of the feature. The RuntimeFeature page and configure-language-version carry the runtime-support claim.

issues.claim: Разделите возможности на две группы ... / Split the features into two groups ...
issues.problem: The hint says two groups, while the explanation describes three (compiler-only, needs missing types, needs CLR changes). The wording 'change how the CLR loads types and calls methods' almost names the answer.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the hint less direct, for example: 'For each feature, ask whether the compiler can lower it to ordinary IL by itself, possibly with helper types you declare yourself, or whether the CLR must understand something new.' Align the group count with the explanation.
